title: Ring-sheaf lift of a finite-limit-preserving inverse image
statement:
Let $(C,J)$ and $(C',J')$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in a common universe. Let
$L:\operatorname{Sh}(C,J,\mathrm{Set})\to\operatorname{Sh}(C',J',\mathrm{Set})$ be left adjoint to
$V:\operatorname{Sh}(C',J',\mathrm{Set})\to\operatorname{Sh}(C,J,\mathrm{Set})$ and assume that $L$ preserves finite limits. There are a functor
$\operatorname{rings}:\operatorname{Sh}(C,J,\mathrm{CommRing})\to
\operatorname{Sh}(C',J',\mathrm{CommRing})$, a right-adjoint ring functor $V_{\mathrm{rings}}$, an adjunction
$\operatorname{rings}\dashv V_{\mathrm{rings}}$, and, for every source ring sheaf $R$, an isomorphism
$e_R:L(|R|)\simeq|\operatorname{rings}.obj(R)|$, where $|{-}|$ is the underlying sheaf of sets.
The isomorphisms $e_R$ are natural in $R$: for every morphism $\varphi:R\to S$ of commutative ring sheaves on $(C,J)$,
$e_S\circ L(|\varphi|)=|\operatorname{rings}(\varphi)|\circ e_R$ as maps $L(|R|)\to|\operatorname{rings}.obj(S)|$.
For every $R$, $e_R$ identifies addition, multiplication, zero, and one of $R$ with the corresponding
operations on $\operatorname{rings}.obj(R)$ through the canonical finite-product and terminal-object
comparisons for $L$. The ring adjunction hom-equivalence, after forgetting rings and using $e_R$, is the
original set-sheaf adjunction hom-equivalence. Here $\operatorname{CommRing}$ and the underlying-sheaf
functors are those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tags 00YV and 03D2: functoriality of algebraic structures under a finite-limit-preserving inverse image

proof.text: Write A = Sh(C,J,Set) and B = Sh(C',J',Set). The existing sheaf algebraic-structures equivalence identifies sheaves of commutative rings on each site with commutative ring objects in A and B, and its composites with the internal-object forgetful functors are the ordinary underlying-sheaf functors. Thus it is legitimate to construct the lift on internal commutative ring objects and transport it back to ring sheaves.

Apply the adjunction-lifts-group-ring-objects theorem to L ⊣ V. Its finite-product hypothesis is exactly the assumed preservation of finite limits, so finite products and the terminal object are preserved. The theorem supplies lifted functors on commutative ring objects, a lifted adjunction, the underlying functor equalities, and the operation-transport equations for addition, zero, negation, multiplication and one.

source.place: Tag 00YV, construction of algebraic structures under a finite-limit-preserving inverse image

proof.text: Transport the lifted functors and their adjunction across the two sheaf/ring-object isomorphisms from Step 1. Call the transported functors rings and V_rings. The underlying functor equality for the lifted left functor gives, at each source ring sheaf R, an isomorphism e_R : L(|R|) ≅ |rings.obj(R)|. Because it is the component of a functor equality, e_R is natural in every ring morphism. The operation-transport equations from Step 2, transported through the sheaf/ring-object isomorphisms, say exactly that e_R identifies addition, multiplication, zero and one (and the additive inverse) with the canonical finite-product and terminal-object comparisons for L.

source.place: Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi): the discussion before it (structure maps transported through f^{-1}, which commutes with finite limits) and the proof of (2), rings as sextuples

proof.text: The lifted adjunction hom-equivalence in Step 2 transports across the same isomorphisms, so rings ⊣ V_rings. Under the underlying-sheaf identifications and e_R, its hom bijection is the original L ⊣ V hom bijection. Naturality of e and the transported operation equations give the stated ring naturality and operation clauses, while the transported unit and counit are the units and counits of the ring adjunction. This proves every clause of the assertion.
